utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. I have to apologise for the delay since it is very difficult to find the time for the whole Trial Chamber to have a meeting, so we had one at 8.00 this morning, so -- which caused a delay for this sitting for five minutes. I apologise to everybody. Well, Witness, good morning. Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Good morning. I am ready, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Chana: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, yesterday we were at Zuka's base and you were telling us about the reaction of those assembled when you told them the story of the children and what they had told you about the murder of their families. Now, I'd like to take you to -- this is at page 85 of the transcript yesterday when you said: "Mr. Sefer Halilovic and everybody else assembled there was that they didn't want to hear anything about the children and the children should be removed and that dirty laundry ought to be removed." Now, can you tell me -- can you elaborate as to what you -- what was meant by "dirty laundry should be removed."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that it was stated that dirty laundry should be hidden, and dirty laundry means that all those things that had happened should be concealed actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was that going to be concealed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after the crime in Grabovica, an order was issued. Mr. Halilovic and Zulfikar Alispago issued the order to set up a checkpoint somewhere at the bridge, because those who managed to flee the massacre had already reached Jablanica and the information was already out about the crime. There was already talk about the crime and some things were already out in the open. Some journalists and police and UNPROFOR who were active in that area of responsibility had already started to move towards Grabovica, and the checkpoint was then set up at the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to come to the checkpoints in a minute. But before we do that, I would still like to take you back to Zuka's base, if I may, because it's important for Their Honours to understand what was said and by whom. And if you can now please cast your mind back and tell us, who said that the children should be removed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the base --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, what the witness said was that "dirty laundry should be removed" and he gave an explanation of what that meant. In terms of removing the children, if that's what the witness says, he can say it himself. But that's not what he said up to now. The question says that very thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the children should be removed and dirty laundry ought to be removed, all this was said by this witness himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So the Prosecution will clarify it on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who said it.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when I arrived at the base -- actually, at the point in time when I arrived at the base, almost everybody was in favour of removing the children so that there would be no witnesses to the crime. All those who were in the office, from Sefer Halilovic to his other assistants, Zuka, all of them were saying that I shouldn't have even brought the children to the office and that the children should be removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "removed," could you be clear about that. What was meant?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the children were supposed to end up in the same way that their parents and their family ended up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was a decision made not to allow the kids to go back to Jablanica? As you said yesterday, they had indicated that they had relatives there.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the conversation I had with them, they themselves told me that they had an aunt and an uncle in Jablanica. The children themselves wanted to go there. They knew that everyone from their family was killed, so of course they were looking for somebody, a relative where they could find shelter. They wanted to go to Jablanica to their aunt and uncle's, but they were not allowed to do that. A decision was made at Zuka's base that the children could not leave Zuka's base but that they should remain at this base, at the command where Zuka's soldiers were also staying, for as long as the offensive lasted. I tried several times to suggest to those people that these are underaged children, minors. They were about 10 or 9 years old at the time, and that the children had to be sent or must be sent to Jablanica, that it wasn't good for them to be in the barracks. But this decision was not made. All of those who were present in the command decided that the children should stay at the command and sleep there. I would also like to point out that they were interviewed by an independent journalist who happened to be there. His name was Sefko Hodzic. He was the first person to take a statement from them. They told him everything about the crime, what had happened to them and to members of their family. And in spite of that, Sefko Hodzic also did not state anything to anybody publicly. He did not publish what the children said and the children were not sent to Jablanica to their relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, you said that it was decided that they must stay at Zuka's base as long as the offensive lasted, and that's at page [sic] 13. Why did they have to stay in Zuka's base as long as the offensive lasted?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was said at the time that the news should not get out. As I said, the dirty laundry had to be concealed, the crime had to be concealed, and the offensive that was to start in a few days also had to be concealed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the offensive had to be concealed? Is that what you said? I'm just clarifying.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the offensive was supposed to start in a few days' time, but if the children left for Jablanica that would be known, become known. So that's why they had to keep the children there. That's what they thought, the children had to be kept in the barracks so that the offensive that was supposed to begin in a few days should be concealed from the public.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that the children went inside that room where all were assembled and also talked --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the boys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And they went and gave the full story as to what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, one of the boys. Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After one of the boys had talked to the assembled, what was the reaction then? And I would like you to concentrate on Sefer Halilovic's reaction as well as the others, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reaction, especially that of Mr. Sefer Halilovic, naturally -- well, he did listen to the children up to a point. He heard them out, and he didn't say anything when the boy was here. Once the boy went out, then they said that what had happened had to be concealed. They spoke about keeping the children in the base, that they should not be allowed to go to Jablanica, and that the crime should be concealed, and not only Mr. Halilovic but the others also said more or less the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, let's go to these checkpoints. Who ordered the checkpoints be placed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after that, Mr. Sefer Halilovic ordered Zuka to set up a checkpoint from the Jablanica towards Mostar. When you are crossing from the right to the left bank of the Neretva, there was a concrete bridge. A checkpoint was set up there, manned by a number of Zuka's men, including some members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, I will show you another picture. This is 65 ter number 147, 0299-2346. It will come up on your screen in a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 417.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the picture now, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this picture is of, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph here depicts the bridge, and you can see where the checkpoint was set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please take, as you did yesterday, and mark with a circle where the checkpoint was established.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please write there "checkpoint."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you, with broken arrows, indicate to Their Honours where the direction of Grabovica would be, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And would you put "Grabovica" at the end of that arrow, please. Would you write in "Grabovica."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why was it thought fit to put a checkpoint at this particular place?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The checkpoint was set up primarily in order to prevent the journalists, police, and UNPROFOR from going into Grabovica. There was already talk about the crime, and I personally saw when I was passing by the checkpoint a white transporter standing there. It had been stopped. A journalist, I don't know her name but I think that she was of Jewish origin who wanted to get to Grabovica. The police from Jablanica also tried to get through, but they didn't manage to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was this checkpoint sufficient to secure the village?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The checkpoint wasn't meant to secure the village. There was nothing to secure it from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the purpose of the checkpoint, as you said, to stop people from going in. So did it serve its purpose?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason why it was set up was to prevent the entry of certain organs that could find out something about the crime. This would be the police from Jablanica but also the UNPROFOR and journalists, and it did serve its purpose, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said Zuka's men were manning this particular checkpoint. How many were they at this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About three or four fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other checkpoint established nearer the village or in the village, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a normal occurrence to have guards any place where there are soldiers. In the village itself when the soldiers were billeted there, guardposts were set up. Zuka's command decided, and this was conveyed to the unit commanders and since the offensive was going to begin in a few days soldiers were not supposed to go into town, they were not supposed to get drunk because if they get drunk then they would cause problems, and that is why these guardposts were set up. Nobody else was talking about setting up any checkpoints after the crime. These guardposts were set up immediately, as soon as the soldiers were billeted in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I would like to introduce this into evidence, MFI 417. 20

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original of the photograph is Prosecution Exhibit P417 and the one that's marked will be Prosecution Exhibit P418.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, how many soldiers would you say were in the village at this time, an estimation, please?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, there were about 150, maybe more, fighters; however, there were usually more because there were people coming from the other units. A couple of kilometres from the village there was the line where the attacks were supposed to take place. So there were always more soldiers from the 10th Mountain Brigade, from some other units, from Zuka's units. They would come to spend time, socialise, with the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge were any arrests made of any soldiers at this time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was Zuka's unit, under whom these soldiers were subordinated, sufficiently equipped to have made such arrests if they had wanted to?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, there wasn't any talk about any arrests. I was present at the meeting there. There was no mention of arrests. The other thing is, if they wanted to arrest anyone, they could have done that very easily. These were soldiers, but most of the soldiers who were billeted in Grabovica were not in favour of this. And I'm sure that they and all the others, had they wanted to locate these soldiers, it would have been very easy to arrest them. But there was no mention of any arrests. And I think that if anybody says that they did anything towards that end, would be lying -- they would be lying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, whose duty was it to order the arrests of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It better be specified which soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, whose duty would it have been to order the arrest of any of the perpetrators of these crimes?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It first would be the duty of Mr. Sefer Halilovic to order Zuka, because that happened on his axis of command. So it would be the duty of Mr. Sefer Halilovic to issue an order to Zulfikar to undertake measures, to conduct an investigation, and to find out the perpetrators of the crime. Then it would have been easy to arrest them. But I repeat, it wasn't in anyone's interest and nobody did anything towards that end. Nobody was even interested in that crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your own information at the time, when do you think the killings -- which date do you think the killings happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, before that question is answered, we've got no notice that this witness was going to say anything about this. And it had better be established exactly what it was that was the basis of the witness's knowledge before he gives an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, from the previous questions and answers, we know that the witness came to a certain place and spent the night. When he came back from that place to Zuka's headquarters, he heard what happened in Grabovica. So I believe this question is the follow-up from those questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honour's right, then that's correct. But the basis -- if he's being asked for an opinion as to when he thinks it takes place, then he -- the basis for that opinion has to be sought before it's -- it's led, otherwise it's just a speculative opinion that's got no value in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think this is a speculative opinion on this point, because there's some background on that. Let's see what the Prosecution will lead to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. I think it was built in my question when I said "according to your information at the time."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Delalic, would you tell us -- would you answer -- do you need reminding?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those killings occurred in the night, starting from the moment when it began to get dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would be the date of that night?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The night of the 8th to the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how do you know this? How did you know it at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people spoke about that. Since I found out about it, I was told on the base that a crime had been committed in the night. And later on on a number of occasions, people talked about the crime and about the time when these crimes had been committed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you have any information as to where Sefer Halilovic was on that night?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because he was in Zuka's base in the early morning, and it wasn't possible for him to go anywhere further in order to be able to return so early in the morning to the base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would it not have been possible for him to have returned so early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I think that the road from Jablanica to Konjic had been blocked or part of the road after -- the exit from Konjic to Jablanica was under Croatian control. So I doubt he would have taken the risk of going from Jablanica to Konjic to sleep there and then return immediately in the morning. Secondly, there is a byroad, a circular road, which is a lot more longer and difficult. I don't believe he could have returned from Konjic to Jablanica so early. I'm referring to Konjic now. In the direction of Mostar, the road was also blocked, so I believe he was in Jablanica. But in any event, he was in Zuka's base in the early morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long is the road from Konjic to Jablanica and how long would it take to travel down that road at that time, given the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the road from Konjic to Jablanica is not very long. It takes perhaps half an hour to get there if the conditions were normal. However, as I have already said, there was a checkpoint or there were Croatian soldiers who were checking vehicles. So it was impossible to pass through, to go from Jablanica to Konjic or from Konjic to Jablanica. However, if you used the dirt road I have mentioned, which is a sort of circular road, it would have taken three or four hours or even longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, you must have over the time, since these murders were committed, talked to various soldiers. First of all, let me ask: Did you talk to your soldiers over time about these killings?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All soldiers that one attempted to speak to were scared in a certain sense. No one wanted to know anything about this and they all dissociated themselves from the event. No one wanted to say anything about it. However, certain things came to light, certain information could be obtained. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why, Mr. Delalic, in your view did these murders take place?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said at the beginning, it was stupid to billet the men in a village inhabited by Croats. The inhabitants were all Croats in the village; there were no Bosniaks. And in the immediate vicinity of that village, there was the defence line manned by Croatian soldiers. It was quite possible that some Bosniak soldiers might be killed. One should have taken into account the possibility of revenge being taken of soldiers acting out of vengeance if family members of theirs were killed. One should also bear in mind that given the inhabitants who lived there, if they knew that their people were being attacked, certain conflicts would have occurred between the inhabitants and the soldiers. So this should have been foreseen, and the men, the soldiers, certainly should not have been billeted in that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whose decision it was to billet these soldiers in this village?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume this decision was taken by the superior command. They decided about everything and they decided about billeting the men there, too. So I couldn't say who took the decision for sure, but we know who took the decisions and who planned the action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you returned from the village for the second time when you saw these checkpoints, did you have occasion to speak to Sefer Halilovic about what -- your findings again?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had contact on a number of occasions, but we didn't speak about this again. The decision was taken and no one paid much attention to the crime itself afterwards or to anything else. Everyone was focussed on the upcoming offensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do yourself? Did you remain in the area? Did you go back to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the crime, I stayed there for a day or two. I was supposed to reach an agreement with Zuka about taking charge of the materiel and technical equipment that I had bought from him. But I was told it was only after the offensive that I would be able to take charge of that materiel, and I then returned to Sarajevo. As the order was that the troops should remain there for about seven days, I was again issued an oral order, which I received from Mr. Karavelic. I was told that I had to leave Jablanica and return the troops. But as the offensive was late in starting, it wasn't possible to return by that deadline. The troops had to remain down there, I would say, for about another ten days.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Just give me a minute please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned to Sarajevo, did you report what you had heard about and knew about the crimes in Grabovica to your superior command there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, while I was still in Jablanica information was obtained about the crime and an order arrived from the supreme command. We were ordered to stop with the offensive and to make objective assessments about the offensive, and we were ordered to identify the perpetrators of the crime and arrest them. I saw Mr. Sefer Halilovic and Zulfikar Alispago tearing up the order. They reacted very angrily to the order and Sefko Hodzic was present at the time. He had taken a statement from the children, and he was present when the order arrived. But in spite of the fact, he did not publish any articles about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to come to -- in a minute to that order, but I would like to please maintain the chronology. Now, did your troops go back to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they returned, but it took them longer to return than had been planned. They stayed down there for about 15 days, I don't know for how long exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at some documents now. I'd like to show you P388. Can you see the document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- it's dated 12th of September, 1993, and it's from Karavelic to Halilovic. What is the meaning of this document, could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the corps command in Sarajevo and in the supreme command, they already knew about the crime. And the corps commander ordered that the units should return to Sarajevo in order to question the men or do something like that. But this order was not carried out, and the troops did not return to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is Vahid Karavelic's order to ask the troops to return, and this order was not carried out. Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the offensive that had been planned had not yet been launched. And the superior command in Jablanica did not allow this to be carried out. Sefer Halilovic and Zulfikar Alispago were against this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was there -- how did they countermand this order so these troops did not return to Sarajevo, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this order was never even forwarded to the men. They received the order, but they did not act on it. They didn't show it to anyone. So the troops' commander knew nothing about the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to show D157 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, just a moment. Before that happens, is my learned friend going to ask whether this witness saw this order at the time? Otherwise, what's the basis of showing it to him at all? That question simply hasn't been asked yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But first of all I have to ask whether this document has been admitted into the evidence or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It's -- the previous one, yes. P388, Your Honour. It's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So you may ask a question following the line put by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw this order, this one on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this order as soon as it arrived. Mr. Sefer Halilovic and Zulfikar Alispago and some other members of the staff were in front of the base when the order arrived. Mr. Sefko Hodzic was also present. As soon as they had read it, they just tore it up and threw it away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the order that they tore up? Because I'd like to show you another order and I'll come back to that as well because we can only show one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: If we can please have D157 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see it? There's another order on your screen. Now, this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't want Mr. Karkin making audible comments, Your Honours, during the changeover of these documents. Now, it just happened right then and I object to it. I'll have a matter of law to raise in the break about this, Your Honours, but there was an audible comment made there. I don't know what it was myself, but we can't have that sort of thing going on. I was watching and I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There is some leading elements in your questions, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will correct that immediately. Your Honour, it's just that I'm limited by the technology because I would like to have two orders. This is the kind of time when e-court doesn't do us justice because it's important that we see both orders together. If I could show them to him in paper form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, the witness has before him P388, which is currently on our screens, and D157.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are two orders and they are both dated 12th September, 1993. So could you please look at both of them and then I will ask you questions. One is from Karavelic to Halilovic, and the other one is from Rasim Delic to the supreme command to Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, this is not an order that I had seen. But I knew that it had arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly. So 388 you had not seen at the time it arrived in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at D157. Tell us about this order.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just referring to this order that arrived when we were in front of Zulfikar Alispago's base. Mr. Sefer Halilovic was there and his assistants; members of the Main Staff; Zulfikar Alispago; myself; the independent journalist, Sefko Hodzic. Everyone saw the order. Everyone knew about its contents. The offensive had not been launched. Sefer Halilovic and his staff and Zulfikar Alispago were very angry about this. So they reacted in this angry manner and tore the order up, threw it away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who tore the order up and threw it away?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Sefer Halilovic first crumpled it, then Zuka raised it from the ground, read it through, laughed, and tore it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it about in order that they did not like?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they told us what the order was about. They said that it was to assess the objective possibility of carrying out this attack and the possibility of arresting the perpetrators of the crime, and this is something that they did not like.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Perhaps Your Honours can have this D157 on their screens. Is it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Chana, it's on the screen, D157.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the first one. Rasim Delic is ordering Sefer Halilovic in point one: "Re-examine the decision in the sense of a realistic estimate of forces and possibilities of carrying out the tasks. In accordance with that, amend the decision so that it conforms to real possibilities." What does that mean to you, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 1 of the order, the sentence is about this: "Re-examine the decision in a sense of a realistic estimate of forces and possibilities of carrying out the tasks." This is meaning to see whether our forces were sufficiently well equipped for the task; I don't think they were and this was subsequently proven to be true. There was nothing we could do. And it says, in accordance with that: "Amend the decision so that it conforms with real possibilities." This means stop the offensive or reduce it to a minimum. Just carry out the tasks that could be carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was being asked to do this, to re-examine? Who is it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sefer Halilovic himself received this order, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at number 2 where it says: "Check the accuracy of information regarding the genocide committed against the civilian population by the members of the 1st Corps, 9th Motorised Brigade. If the information is correct, isolate the perpetrators and take energetic measures. Do everything to prevent such actions. Order the 1st Corps, 9th deputy commander to return to Sarajevo immediately in order to solve the problems in the unit." What was now being asked of Mr. Halilovic by his commander in this, point 2?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is being asked to check the accuracy of the information, or rather -- or rather, to look into the crime that had been committed in Grabovica, and if possible, to identify the perpetrators and arrest them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 3 he is now commanded to: "Immediately inform me about the measures that have been taken and tasks that have been carried out." I think that speaks for itself, but I will ask you this: When Mr. Halilovic crumpled this order, did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the order we have before us shows what should have been down; however, nothing was done after the order had been received. The only reaction was anger and curses addressed to Rasim Delic and the president of the Presidency. No one else mentioned arresting the soldiers who may have committed this crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you see any intention whatsoever to obey this order from his superior command?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did your troops actually return to Sarajevo? What date was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the offensive had been completed. The offensive was launched a few days later; it lasted for several days. And around the 21st or 22nd, I don't remember the exact date, the troops returned to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there when the troops were ready to go back to Sarajevo from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed that the troops were ready to return. I was moving between Konjic and Jablanica. Several times I went to the entrance to Sarajevo and to Sarajevo itself. When I was informed that the offensive had been completed, I went to the base where Sefer Halilovic was. The troops were ready. They were in lorries and ready to return. And Sefer Halilovic said that all these units should be careful about being captured at the entrance to the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why is it that he said that to you, that your unit should be careful?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he repeated that it was necessary to conceal the laundry and -- he said that the laundry should be concealed and that when entering Sarajevo, or rather while travelling from Jablanica to Sarajevo they should be careful, they should take care to avoid capture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he inform you that -- about where this possible capture might take place?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the entrance to the tunnel that was beneath the airport Tarmac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did Sefer warn you about this possible capture of your troops?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because of the crime that had been committed, apparently. And at the time they didn't know which men had committed the crime. So this wasn't told just to the troops from the 9th Mountain Brigade; it was also told to other troops from the 10th Mountain Brigade, et cetera. Everyone was told that when entering Sarajevo they should make sure they were not checked, controlled, arrested, et cetera, et cetera, and this is what they were -- they were told such things because of the crime that had been committed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be quite clear about this, who were they to be captured by? Who was it that might capture them?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably the 1st Corps command, the military police, the 1st Corps military police, or rather the military security service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the 1st Corps commander, Vahid Karavelic, say anything to you when you had sort of gone back to Sarajevo about the possibility of these arrests?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you another document, which is P389. It's an order dated 23rd of September, 1993. Now, were your troops back in Sarajevo as of that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you look at the order? Is it in your -- on your screen. It's an order from Halilovic to Karavelic. What is this order requesting Karavelic --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this order?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order forwarded to Vahid Karavelic, the commander of the 1st Corps, to immediately start organising and preparing three companies consisting of 100 soldiers from their composition which are to be sent to the Vrdi front. Again, they were asking about the same orders that had been asked on the 3rd of September or the 7th of September. The order was to send units to the same place in order to carry out combat activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So briefly, the soldiers were being asked to go back, some soldiers, to be deployed back to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object to that. Your Honours, that's -- just excuse me a moment, please. Your Honours, there is no comment about any soldiers going back. Whether it was to be the same soldiers or not is not this witness's evidence at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to pursue this issue, Ms. Chana, you have to law some foundations for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at item 1 of the order. Halilovic orders Karavelic and says: "The 1st Corps command will immediately start preparing and ordering three companies consisting of 100 soldiers from their composition which are to be sent to the Vrdi front." Where was Vrdi?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vrdi is in the -- on the axis commanded -- under the command of Zulfikar Alispago from the previous offensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there is no -- Sefer Halilovic asks for 100 soldiers. It is not specified as to which soldiers. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, this order was quite strange. It was quite strange to issue such an order. In my opinion, the crime that happened down there should have been investigated first. But now we have the soldiers being sent to -- or a request for the soldiers to be sent to the Jablanica sector in order to carry out new combat activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were they going to be subordinated to this time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Zulfikar Alispago also, I think, because that was his sector there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zulfikar Alispago was subordinated to whom?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfikar Alispago was the commander of the Sjever dva, North 2 group. So he was subordinated to Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I'll show you another document now, please. That's P395. This is an order dated 24th September 1993 from Commander Vahid Karavelic to your brigade, and attention Ramiz Delalic. Is it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how does this order start? Does it say: "Following the order given by chief of supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," and then it asks you "immediately to commence organisational and materiel preparation for 105-strong company to be dispatched to Vrdi, Jablanica sector." Did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you implement this order?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you sent some troops back?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever heard about the IKM?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the IKM?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a forward command post. An IKM was located at Zuka's base, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the IKM set up to do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An IKM is a forward command post. The commander of the operation commands the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that happen, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where would orders come from, from Jablanica, from the IKM, or from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Jablanica IKM.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Operation Neretva commanded from that IKM, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you to another topic altogether, and that is Trebevic 2. What do you know about Trebevic 2?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of Trebevic operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Trebevic 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It was a settling of accounts with all units that were not in the -- under the command service or that were not those units which were allegedly criminal units which were not part of the units under the command of Rasim Delic and so on and so forth. T2 happened in Sarajevo. Part of the 9th Motorised Brigade and myself, members of the 9th Motorised Brigade and I myself were arrested, amongst others. There were arrested members as well as the commander of the Delta unit, people from the 10th Mountain Brigade, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what date would this be?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before this arrest and Trebevic 2 attack on your soldiers, had you had occasion to talk to Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On several occasions. In the last month or so, I was constantly in touch with Mr. Sefer Halilovic directly or indirectly, and he expressed concerns about being arrested and he felt that we also could be arrested and that those commanders that had participated in the Neretva 93 operation as well as certain commanders who sent fighters there could also be arrested. So throughout that last month, we were constantly receiving warnings from Mr. Sefer Halilovic, who constantly kept us in a state of expectation that we would be attacked at any time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was Sefer Halilovic giving you these continuous warnings and keeping you in a state of expectation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think primarily because of himself. He expected to be arrested himself and replaced. In order to keep things the way they were, he had to have supporters. He also gave such warnings to Mr. Zulfikar Alispago, Zuka, and to units stationed around Mostar as well as those stationed in Sarajevo. To me, the 10th Mountain Brigade, the Independent Battalion, the Delta unit, and other units were receiving these warnings that you would be attacked, you would be arrested, you would be killed, and so on and so forth. After that warning, I went to see the president personally. I also went to the commander of the armed forces, Rasim Delic. I went to the security services also. I tried to find out something about this, and I was told that this was not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did Mr. Halilovic at any time advise you as to what to do if you were indeed attacked?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On several occasions he would come or he would send somebody to pick us up so that we would go and see him. There was a fighter of Zuka's, his name was Mesar, and he was also an escort and driver for Mr. Halilovic. There was also another person called Vid or something like that who was part of his security force. They would come and pick us up to take us to meet Mr. Sefer Halilovic, to meet with him and talk. Then they would say, You would be attacked the next day, we would be attacked tomorrow, you would be attacked at such-and-such a time. And they would say, You have to defend yourself, you have to shoot directly into the flesh, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did it mean to you, that you have to shoot directly into the flesh?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That meant that we had to shoot at those who attacked us.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to now play an intercept, which is 65 ter 103 -- is 0147-2927. We will listen to the audio via Sanction, Your Honour, and I would like to state that I've been informed, very reliably from my case manager, that the interpretation might be quite fast and to make sure that Your Honours can listen to it. The audio will be quite fast. You may please indicate at any time to slow it down or stop or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let's try that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have the transcript available?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It's on the screen, Your Honour, the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 419.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, would you please listen to this audio transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, whose voices are there that you recognise, if you do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the voices. The voices are mine and Mr. Sefer Halilovic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what date was this conversation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of October at sometime in the morning, perhaps at around 8.30 or 9.00 in the morning. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the day that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this before the soldiers had come, this conversation took place before?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whose soldiers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You, yourself, I'm sorry. The other soldiers who came to arrest you.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was -- they had already come in the morning. And during the night they deployed their people. They carried out the attack against us in the morning, and I immediately called Mr. Sefer Halilovic to find out what exactly was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you arrested for -- sorry. How long were you in custody?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About seven and a half months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you charged?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a conviction entered?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was charged of insubordination to the commander of the 1st Corps and for not executing orders. During the attack I was supposed to surrender the barracks, and for that I was sentenced to three and a half years in prison. Later, I was pardoned by the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was Sefer Halilovic to your knowledge also arrested?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day or around that day, yes, he was. But I don't know exactly what happened. But he was arrested; he told me that himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we go on to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are the Prosecutors intending to tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I've got two or three to tender and I thought I would tender them all together at the end of the -- this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Morrissey would like to make some comments on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We don't want to interrupt the witness's evidence now. I'm going to indicate that we're going to reserve our position on that, so that can be discussed at the end of the evidence as to whether it should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. You may proceed, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm almost coming to an end here anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, what were your relations with Mr. Halilovic after Trebevic 2?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was good until 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after 1996?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1996 -- well, I think it was 1996. It could have been 1997. An investigator came. He introduced himself as a journalist, but he actually was an investigator. On that occasion, Mr. Sefer Halilovic told me that this is -- an investigator arrived at Sarajevo and that he wanted to interview me. I agreed to that. I asked Mr. Sefer Halilovic what it was that this so-called journalist wanted to talk to me about, but I knew that he was an investigator. And I was told that he wanted to talk about the crime that had taken place in Grabovica. On that occasion, Mr. Sefer Halilovic asked me that if the investigator asked me if an order had been issued by Sefer Halilovic for an investigation to be conducted, to say that, yes, it had been -- that it was issued. I said that I would say so, but when we came to some house in Hrasnica, this was on the outskirts of Sarajevo where this journalist was with his interpreter, I told him what he wanted to know in the statement about Grabovica, but I did not say that the order had been issued and sent, which was true. It had not been issued and sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of this investigator?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes my examination-in-chief of this witness. And as I promised, I've kept within my time frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: But I -- sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Subject of course to introducing these documents into exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we may deal with them at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, yes, I think that's appropriate, Your Honour. I'll take it that the Prosecution are offering the tape and the transcript for tender, and I'll just reserve my position about it and we can deal with that at a later time. But could I just ask before we break that the Prosecutor provide the Defence with a copy of this statement that Mr. Delalic made in 1996 to the investigator or could they confirm that they have it or that it exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: If you would please give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I may clarify, with your permission, with the witness as to whose investigator this was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The statement that you gave, was it a written statement? And whose investigator was it, what you've just discussed.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that he was an investigator of -- I don't know where from, of what. He was a foreigner and he came from some international court. That's how he introduced himself. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he take a recorded statement from you, audio?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will certainly look into this. We, according to us, have handed over all the audio transcripts that were taken. There was one --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it Mr. Nikolai?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This was much earlier, a long time before Nikolai.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: -- we will certainly look into it during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, maybe we could have a break, during which you could make a research on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey, do you have something to say before you cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. It's a bit of a delicate matter, really, and I think I should raise it now before making any allegations or claims. Your Honours, at page 17 of the transcript my learned friend, Ms. Chana, was examining the witness concerning one of two orders. Now, the two orders that were coming along -- that were being dealt with were firstly an order from -- well, it's not really an order but it's being called an order, from Vahid Karavelic asking Mr. Halilovic to send back units to Sarajevo because there was trouble at Sarajevo. And the next document that Ms. Chana proposed to put to the witness was D157 which is the Delic order dated the 12th of the 9th. Now, it was the Prosecution position to ask questions of Mr. Delic -- Mr. Delalic, the witness here, as to what was Sefer Halilovic's reaction to the Karavelic document, there was a Karavelic one, the Delic one. And the witness gave his answers. And then he said at the end of those answers, he said, "Well, Halilovic just disregarded it and tore it up and threw it on the ground." Now, that was potentially problematic, because -- I'm not sure how familiar Your Honours are with the pre-trial material on these statements but I assume there's been some reading of them and what the Prosecution was believing they were going to get was that Mr. Halilovic tore up the Delic order. But now the witness was saying that he's torn up the Karavelic order. At that moment -- that was when I jumped up because at that moment Mr. Karkin made an audible noise. I don't know what he said. I don't know if it was a word or an exclamation. I'm not going to make -- give any opinion about that. He looked towards the witness and he moved physically. I can't say what the witness saw, whether the witness saw him at all. The witness's back was to me and his head was turned that way. But I'm not asserting anything about that at all, whether the witness saw it. Now, the action by Mr. Karkin might bear a number of interpretations. I don't know what was in his mind. I don't know whether he was trying to communicate with the witness or whether it was just a spontaneous exclamation. And I ought to be very slow to make an allegation against a lawyer who's here performing a function at the permission of the Court. But I'm very concerned by it, frankly. I saw it, I raised it immediately because I saw it, and I want to now raise this. I don't -- I submit that he shouldn't be in the court. There's a real concern if that sort of thing is going to be repeated and it really raises a question as to what involvement he is to have here. As I understand it, a witness like Mr. Delalic who's on any view of things -- he's a suspect from the Prosecutor's point of view, he's named in the indictment as a burier of bodies or an order of it. So it's quite clear he may from time to time be in danger of incriminating himself and it might be that he needs advice. But the practice of this Tribunal I think in the past has been a flexible one, tailored to circumstances, and it's not constrained by common law rules or by civil law rules. It's one that you decide on. In this instance it seems to me appropriate to submit that this witness is intelligent and well-informed about the case against him, and you would well imagine that he would be. He knows when he's likely to be in trouble or when he might be likely to incriminate himself and he will know when he needs legal advice. It's really for the witness to assert the privilege; it's not for the lawyer to do so. Now, Mr. Karkin could well be permitted to remain in the environment of the court in one of the rooms out there and be on call if needed to come and give advice and give appropriate counselling. At the moment, you know, I'm not prepared to make an assertion against him because I don't know what was in his mind, but what he did was unmistakable. It was seen by Mr. Mettraux as well, and it was just too clear to be unmistaken. So what he meant by that, I don't know. But it just came at a moment when the witness made, according to the Prosecution's theory, a mistake. Because he gave a wrong answer. He was supposed to be tearing up the other order. Now he said that he tore up the Karavelic order and then there was a sudden clearing of the throat and a word or noise happened. And then you got the answer changed. And it, yeah, it really is a concern to me. As I say, I'm not here to make allegations against Karkin. I don't know what was happening there, but I don't want it to happen again. I'm very concerned by it. I can't complain later, so I complain now. And it seems to me appropriate that he should be in the court in those circumstances. But the Prosecution should be entitled to be heard about that and perhaps Mr. Karkin could be heard about it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Any response?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I think that from what my perception of what happened is that the witness was shown two orders. And what happened was while I was referring to one there was another one on the screen. As I said, I couldn't show both together. The witness was very clear that the Karavelic order he had never seen before; it was the Delic order. And because they're both 12th September and the purport of both the orders is the same, he immediately said, yes, that's the one he saw torn up. I believe from what I've heard from our case manager who was sitting next to him, Sandra, and who had an opportunity to observe Mr. Karkin is that it was kind of an impulsive reaction from him to say, no it's -- you haven't got the right order on the screen. Either -- the witness had one order on the screen; I started talking about another one. So to that extent I'll take the blame that the different orders were shown at different times, because I would have liked to have the witness shown both together, because sometimes it happens that it's imperative that the witness see two together. But it was quite clear from the witness's evidence, Your Honour, at line 17 he says: "I did not see the Karavelic order." And all along it is the Rasim Delic order which was -- which he had seen torn up and crumpled. And Mr. Karkin's reaction, I think, was an impulsive one because he understood, as did our case managers, that the witness was looking at the wrong order on the screen because they both were very -- one was based on another, so very similar contents of both orders. If the witness had said he'd seen both at the time, then quite -- learned counsel is quite right, that there is a possible confusion. One he had not seen before, the Karavelic order, it was only the Rasim Delic. And I think the witness himself was a little confused. I'm sure this matter can be clarified with the witness during cross-examination, but I take Mr. Morrissey's point that it's perturbing to have these things happen. Now, in respect of Mr. Karkin's participation in these proceedings, he was given permission by Your Honours to -- to sit in there. His role is one of purely if any advice is needed by the witness at any time in the proceedings, it's appropriate Mr. Karkin sit in and hear what's happening, so if the witness was to request some advice, whether he should answer a question on grounds that he might rather not answer a question, on grounds it might incriminate him. So I think this is the first time Mr. Karkin had an involuntary reaction. And I'm sure duly warned by the Court, he will be very mindful in the future that even if there is what appears to be an error on the part of myself and the witness, that he will leave it to me to clarify it in my own good time. To that extent, Your Honour, I feel that Mr. Karkin is not somebody who should be barred from these proceedings because on one occasion he tried to point out that the witness was looking at the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. A very short, concise reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it will be short and concise, but it's relevant. My learned friend would be a very good defence advocate I must say, and she's done a very good job in defence of Mr. Karkin. If the Court looks at page 16, please, on the transcript you'll see how the questioning unfold and it really isn't -- it doesn't bear the Defence [sic] interpretation that my learned friend's put on it. You'll see at the top of page 16 that Karavelic -- the question -- the order that's referred to is -- is at line 2: "Can you -- it's dated 12th September, 1993, and it's from Karavelic to Halilovic. What's the meaning of this document. Can you please tell us." That document was the one on the screen, of course. And then -- the witness then gives an explanation. He ends up saying: "It was not carried out and the troops did not return to Sarajevo." My friend then asks: "So this is Vahid Karavelic's orders to ask the troops to return" - and this is not to carry that - "do you know why." And then an answer is then given. "Well, the offensive had been planned and not yet been launched" and so on. And the witness says: "Sefer Halilovic and Zulfikar Alispago are against this." So they are talking about the Karavelic order. There's nothing, there is no ambiguity whatsoever. At that point, there's none. It's clearly about that order and nothing else. Then we go on to the next question: "So how did they counter this order?"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down, Mr. Morrissey, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm being asked by the people to slow down there. "How did they counter this order? "This order was never even forwarded on to the men." And then I interrupted and asked the question and it had to be made clear -- I asked -- asked that it had not -- be made clear what the situation was about that order. And the witness then went on to say -- sorry, Your Honour then asked that Ms. Chana clarify the matter. And D157, you'll recall, was shown in hard copy. And you will recall that was done. D388 [sic] was the one that was on the screen, it was the Karavelic order on the screen at all times. So then at line -- at page 17, line 10 the question is at line 10: "When was the first time you saw this order, this one on the screen now?" "I saw this as soon as it arrived," et cetera, et cetera, et cetera, "when Sefko Hodzic was also was present. As soon as I'd read it they tore it up and threw it away." Now, we're talking about the one that's on the screen, and the witness gave an answer. The one that's on the screen, that is he said "they tore it up and threw it away." Now it may be that the witness is mistaken. It may be that he's not. It may be -- there could be all sorts of -- of explanations. But Mr. Hodzic's response can't be explained by saying it's the wrong one on -- sorry, not Mr. Hodzic. I'm -- I'm -- take that back. Mr. Karkin's response can't be explained in the way that was said. But in any event, Your Honours, it's a matter for the Tribunal, how you deal with it. I have to be concise now. It's in reply. I ask that he not be permitted to be in here. But in the alternative, I ask that the Court give him a clear warning as to the limits that he's allowed to participate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. Well, I believe that the decision made by this Trial Chamber to have Mr. Delalic's counsel present in these proceedings is to give him the opportunity to follow what is going on in this courtroom; meanwhile, we know that the delicate situation of this witness, Mr. Delalic. So if there's any legal matters that the witness would like to consult his counsel, the counsel is well-informed and will come to the rescue of this witness as soon as possible. And I believe that on the Defence part, there's only some suspicions on that. And it is an allegation on this matter. At this moment, it's difficult for this Bench to know exactly what Mr. Karkin said at that time. So we'll observe the following proceedings. In the meantime, I'll warn the counsel of Mr. Delalic only to see the behaviour of him in the following proceedings. I believe in the cross-examination, there will be some issues that will come up which might come to some disputes. It is so decided at this stage. And another matter is that yesterday we have received a courtesy copy from the Prosecution concerning of the testimony of the expert witness. I wonder whether Defence has received that filing?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm instructed that we've received something on the e-mail this morning. I haven't seen it myself yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you are not in the position to make any response at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I'd -- no, Your Honour, I must say I had other things on my mind. But I'm -- yes, I mean, as soon as court is finished today, of course I'll go and look and see what we've received and I will be able to say what I can tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because there are some logistic arrangements that have to be made. So I hope you could orally give your response as early as possible, maybe tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't believe I'd have a difficulty responding to whatever it is the Prosecution say tomorrow morning. I will do that, but I don't know what it says yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And another matter is on the 9th of May, 2005, the Defence filed a motion responding to the Prosecution's motion to tender the record of interview obtained in violation of the Statute and the Rules. This is a confidential annexed filings. I wonder at this stage whether the Prosecution would like to file a reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, we are actually filing something today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, thank you very much. Because we are waiting for your reply so that the Bench will be in a position to make a ruling on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. It's going to be filed today before 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we start the cross-examination, I have a few words to say to Mr. Karkin, the counsel of Mr. Delalic. Mr. Karkin, the Trial Chamber allows you to be present in this proceeding just to give you the opportunity to follow the proceedings. If -- in case your client has some legal issues to ask for your consultations, you may, with the permission of the Bench, come to his help. But however, you are not allowed to make any interventions as well as gestures to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARKIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a lot of respect for lower-level courts, and I have even more respect for this court. I wasn't reacting to his testimony; I was just commenting to myself on the wrong order that had been shown to the witness. But I will do my best to avoid doing this in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since this is an international tribunal and the participants might use different languages, so I believe very few people in this courtroom could understand what you were saying at that time. So there might be some misunderstandings. So I hope you could bear that in mind and don't do anything that might trigger any suspicions on your part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARKIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Well, Mr. Morrissey, you may proceed with your cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P215. Your Honours, this is the report prepared dated 13 September, by Namik Dzankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, while that's being brought up on the screen, did you meet Namik Dzankovic during the course of your time in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard about him but I never met him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you have in front of you now on the screen in the Bosnian language a document dated at Jablanica, 13th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you see the first paragraph there -- do you see that it's marked and addressed to the attention of Jusuf Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that the first paragraph says that "On the 8th of September, 1993, BH Army units from Sarajevo came to the village of Grabovica within the scope of a planned operation towards Mostar. Their command was Ramiz Delalic, also known as Celo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation as to why people were referring to you as the commander of those units on the 13th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was the deputy commander of the 9th Motorised Brigade, and it was not possible for me to be the commander of a unit of about 50 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But just answer my question. What's your explanation for why somebody would say that you were the commander?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no explanation. I don't understand this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could we please turn the page over. It's -- in the English copy we want DD00 -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me one moment. You'll just have to excuse me a moment, please. All right. Could we please show the witness the next page. In the English version it will be the last page; in the Bosnian version it will be the second page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that next page in front of you now, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see a sentence saying this: "Work on the clarification of this case, gathering of operative information on the exact number of dead, how they were murdered, and detection of possible perpetrators has been done in cooperation with [illegible]," there's a bit of missing text, and then "onsite is impossible to carry out because of the large number of units in the Grabovica area, the attitude of units led by Ramiz Delalic, and fear that giving importance to this incident would result in," then there's a gap and then it says, "return of the whole unit to Sarajevo, which would directly endanger the planned action on Mostar." Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's very difficult to read what I have before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. There may be a technical problem, Mr. Delalic. Just wait a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're just going to identify the line so Mr. Delalic can see where it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could furnish a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we may have that, Your Honours. Very well, could we --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, it's on the second page about halfway down. There's an underlining on the left-hand side. The sentence I'm wanting you to go to is the one that says: "Work on the clarification of this case, gathering of operative information on the exact number of dead, how they were murdered, and detection of possible perpetrators." All right, Mr. Delalic, do you have that? It's about 15 lines from the top. It starts with the word "rad."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, now, do you see that -- that on the 13th of September -- just a minute. Do you see that on that date it's being said that investigation is impossible because, among other things, the attitude of units being led by Ramiz Delalic. Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
