utterances.text: Could somebody please me to find it. I really can't find the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps the best would be if you return that to the Defence and we will simply -- we will indicate it.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just take a moment, please, to read that. I'll read it to you so you have an understanding of what's being put. It's being put here that it's being said on that report on the 13th of September: "Work on the clarification of this case, gathering of operative information on the exact number of dead, how they were murdered, and detection of possible perpetrators has been done in cooperation with," and then there's a gap. There's another gap and it says "onsite is currently impossible to carry out because of the large number of units in the Grabovica area, the attitude of units led by Ramiz Delalic, and fear that giving importance to this incident would result in," there's a gap, "return of the whole unit to Sarajevo, which would directly endanger the planned action to Mostar." Now, it's the fact, isn't it, that your units, your men in Jablanica were very hostile to any investigation. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also the fact that you were very hostile to an investigation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you say quite clearly that you did not want there to be an investigation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you say that if there was an investigation, there was a real danger of open clashes between the unit members and persons who would carry out the on-site inspection and possibly try to identify and arrest the perpetrators. Didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you say it in front of three or four witnesses at Zuka's flat on the evening of the 10th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And didn't you say that at an earlier discussion with Sefer Halilovic, that if there was any attempt at an investigation you would simply take the units back to Sarajevo. True or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And didn't you also say that the investigation, any investigation, would endanger the operation to Mostar, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I'll put it again.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have to say sorry to the Defence counsel, Mr. Delalic. I'll just make sure the question is clear, then answer, and we're both doing our job. You said, didn't you, that an investigation would result in the return of the whole unit to Sarajevo. Didn't you say that in Zuka's flat in front of witnesses?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, that document can be returned now. All right, Mr. Delalic. Now, the position for you is this: You know that the case of Grabovica is not closed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that already two men called Hota and Sakrak have been dealt with by the courts in Sarajevo for their parts in killing civilians at Grabovica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know as well that currently being investigated are at least three more individuals, ex-members of the 9th Brigade, named Vlaholjak, Karagic, and Rajkic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also know, don't you, that there is a new war crimes chamber in its early stages in Sarajevo, which has the competence to deal with wartime atrocities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also know that you were from a very early stage a suspect at this Tribunal, and in fact you were interviewed as a suspect by representatives of the Prosecution at this Tribunal. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am prepared to be held responsible for everything that I did, if I did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just deal with the question you're being asked, please. You were dealt with and interviewed as a suspect by the Prosecution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, on one occasion -- well, more than one occasion, you have expressed a concern that one wrong word from you could earn you 20 years imprisonment in The Hague. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never said that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall ever saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say it in a courtroom in Sarajevo in 1999, that one wrong word from you could result in a trip to The Hague for 20 years?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know that you are, yourself, under suspicion for involvement at Grabovica, both in the crime and, more particularly, in the cover-up of that crime. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it is the fact that you covered up that crime, isn't it, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not cover up anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came to that village and you ordered your troops to conceal the traces of the crime. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereafter, you did everything in your power to sabotage the investigation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's the fact, isn't it, that since -- I've just got some brief questions for you now before we commence with the -- with other matters. Since the war -- since the crimes at Grabovica themselves in 1993, you've been imprisoned on three occasions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "imprisoned," I mean you've had to serve sentences of actual imprisonment on three occasions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have also had to -- have you ever left the country on a false passport?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever purchased a machine-gun that was used in the attempt to kill a man named Herenda?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Have you ever purchased a machine-gun or another weapon that was used in an attempt to kill a man named Herenda?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I did buy something similar, and that is the subject of an investigation. So I would not like to say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we'll see about that. The question is: Did you have possession of such a weapon, the weapon that you -- that was used in the crime against Mr. Herenda?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not wish to respond to this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, you have to. So what's the answer?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a problem. Let's turn the microphones off. This is the topic of an investigation that is being conducted in Sarajevo. If we turn the microphones off, then I will respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm -- I've got my doubts about doing that, frankly, and I've -- it's a pragmatic solution, but frankly I don't want this witness being -- availing himself of the private session for reasons of comfort. I'm not sure why and I don't want to cast any aspersions. It may be that he may wishes to speak to his lawyer about this topic now and indicate what his position is. He can refuse to answer it if it's going to incriminate him and then further steps take place, but we need to know what the position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has made it quite clear that this is a matter under investigation for which he might possibly be charged and I think he has very clearly said he does not wish to engage on this particular issue for that reason. And I think that's quite clear from what he has said, because it's not that he refuses to talk about it, it's a matter under investigation. And as a result --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, if I may say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a question of investigation and whether I am involved or not, and I will answer without the microphones. But since someone else is being charged with this crime in Sarajevo, I am not the one who is charged for this crime. But this crime is being investigated and some assistance is being provided in that. So I am not refusing to answer the question; I will answer the question if the microphones are turned off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, maybe we could go to the private session at this stage since this matter will relate to another person. Maybe another person's name will be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And if in the future we see there's no need to keep it in the private session, we could lift the confidentiality of that piece of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour's -- in fact, the witness's answer there provides a good basis for going to the private session, rather like my learned friend, I had inferred that it was of something else. So I agree we can go to private session --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Mr. Delalic said if the Court insists, he is willing to answer the question and the microphones do not have to be turned off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the private session on the same side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me one moment, please. Very well. Could the witness please be shown Defence document DD00-3073. Its 65 ter number is D780(b).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 420.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have on your screen now --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see on the screen there a judgement concerning you, Ramiz Delalic, relating to --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- a crime you committed in the courtroom of Judge Ibrahim Hadzic on the 28th of April, 1999? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in fact guilty of an offence in that court, now, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you explained your criminal record to the Prosecutor, incidentally, you didn't tell her about that one, did you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only talked about those acts that I was sentenced to prison for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's not quite right, is it? Didn't you tell her about crimes where you were acquitted, such as the attempted double murder and the -- the theft before the war?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was also acquitted for this act, it seems to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't seem like that on the face of the record, Mr. Delalic. Do you see the words: "The accused, Ramiz Delalic, son of Jusuf," and other details, "owner of the Karborg [phoen] catering establishment in Sarajevo, married," and these other details we don't need to worry about, "is guilty." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'll have to repeat your answer, the interpreter didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it states that I am guilty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and you were guilty, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not guilty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to take you to some parts of this, and because we're working from an English copy of it we may go slowly in terms of identifying the parts I want to put to you. But if you're being confused or baffled in any way by my questions you're entitled to say, stop, and I need time to work, because I'll warn you in advance these technologies sometimes do cause delays. Very well. Looking at that first page there, do you agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If Your Honours just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that you were dealt with, because having been summoned to the court you told the judge -- you insulted the judge and you said that he didn't know how to do his job. He wasn't authorised to hear you -- sorry, you were not authorised to -- he was not authorised to hear you, that he was an ordinary commie, and then you said something rude concerning Alija Izetbegovic, then you threw files off the Judge's desk, you cursed his mother, and you threatened to kill him. That's what you were found guilty of, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not do that. These are his allegations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Your lawyer, Mr. Karkin, who's present here in court here today was also present for some parts of what happened on this occasion, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karkin was busy in a different office. And when it was all over, he came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please -- could we please go over to the third page in English. Just excuse me, I'm going to try to locate the Bosnian page with more ease. Just excuse me a moment, please. Your Honours, the part I'm going to take the witness to in the English version is on page 3. We are told that on -- it's -- in the Bosnian version it's on page 2 at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you'll be needing to turn over to page 3 as well after that. And when you get to the bottom of your page 2, you just indicate and the court ushers will turn it over for you. Anyway, do you have in front of you now a page saying -- a section saying: "In his defence against bill of indictment number KT559/99 the accused Ramiz Delalic stated," and then it goes on to give details." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in your defence - and if you need to take some time to read this, just tell us and you'll be given that time of course - but in your defence did you say -- did you admit to saying this: "Like hell you will lock me up. Why don't you lock up the Ustashas who slaughtered Muslims? If you were any younger, I'd beat you up." Your Honour, I'm looking ten lines or so down from the top of that paragraph. Was that part of your defence, that you did admit to doing those things?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please put your question. I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Well, do you see here the paragraph says: "In his defence, Ramiz Delalic stated," and then it lists a number of things. What I'm asking you to confirm is: Did you state, did you agree yourself, that you said: "Like hell you'll lock me up. Why don't you lock up the Ustashas who slaughtered the Muslims. If you were any younger, I'd beat you up."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, do you see that written in the text that you have in front of you or do you need to turn the page over?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But your position now is that you never did say that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the bottom of that paragraph in English is some other things that formed part of your defence on that occasion. You may need to turn over the page to see this. Could I just ask you whether on the page you have the word "Alija Izetbegovic" appears at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'll just have to forgive the colourful language here. I'm just reading it from the transcript. Was it part of your defence that -- you denied using the word "Izetbegovic," that you said -- that you admitted that when the judge said that Alija had put him there you responded by saying that comment: "May Alija fuck you." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you threaten to kill the judge or curse his mother?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now could we please turn over -- I'm going to go to another page now. Could we move to page 4 of the English version, and I'll give you some assistance as to which part of the Bosnian it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, it's page 4 of the English and the words I'm going to commences with the words "witness Ibrahim Hadzic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, I think your part will be at the bottom of page 3 and I just ask you to read that. Then when you finish reading that you can move over to page 4 because there's another part there. Do you see the passage beginning "Witness Ibrahim Hodzic"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise. It may be that this has been translated with "Hodzic" in one place or two places. The correct spelling is "Hadzic" in English. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you see that the Court had evidence from the judge himself, Ibrahim Hadzic, that you entered the room in an arrogant way, that you immediately started insulting him by saying that he did not know how to do his job nor was -- was not authorised to question him, was an ordinary commie, and you swore concerning Alija. Do you see those allegations that the judge made?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the truth, isn't it, that's what you did do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do that, not in the way described here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And next of all, didn't you say to this judge that so many Muslims had been killed, you could not understand the rationale for this investigation. You see that passage, first of all, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's true, isn't it, that's what you said to the judge, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's be quite clear which investigation we're talking about. That was -- you were being questioned about the crime at Grabovica, weren't you, on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in the context of being questioned about the crime at Grabovica, didn't you say that, so many Muslims had been killed, you can't understand the rationale for that investigation. Isn't that what you said, in those exact words?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You threatened to kill the judge several times?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm now turning the page over in English to page 5. Could I just inquire, Mr. Delalic, are you near the bottom of your page or are you over the page to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: There's been something confusing all of us on this side. This document which is D00-3083 [sic] are proofing notes for Mr. Enver Hodzic by one of our OTP attorneys, Patricia Sellers taken on 10th of May, 2005. Is that inadvertence? Have they been [inaudible] By the Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To my understanding, this is a judgement -- well, at least to my understanding is a judgement of the municipal court 1, Sarajevo, against Mr. Delalic dated 15th November, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, Your Honour. That's what's supposed to be there. If my friend has identified something that's got in there that shouldn't be there, then we'll take it out, which we will do of course. Is it there? Will Your Honour allow me to clarify whether we've introduced an alien life form into this document. Because if we have, it's wrong, then we'll take it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it would appear that page 2, as numbered here, is a -- an alien -- something alien to the document and should not be there. In other words, when we've scanned it, we've -- we've seemed to have scanned in something that has nothing to do with it. Enver Hodzic is someone who I don't really know about, to be honest. But could we just ask the court to disregard that page. The next page, as you'll see, is numbered properly. It's page 2, so it's evident that a page of some sort has got into the English version that's come through. We're sorry to the Prosecutors. It probably puts them off while they're trying to follow this. I'm sorry that's happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you did not do it intentionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to speak to my lawyer about it, if I could, Your Honour, but, yes. No, my current -- I didn't do it intentionally, that's true, no. So I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's fine, and I totally accept counsel's explanation on that. But I'm absolutely intrigued how Ms. Patricia Seller's proofing notes have come to the possession of the Defence because these are confidential to -- that's another case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's another case. That's a case within a case. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll deal with that in the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's just got to be pointed out, Your Honour, that there's one photocopying machine, Your Honour, and six defence teams including Mr. Milosevic's team down there, so things happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, please accept my apologies for that delay. Now, could we just come back to this document here. The witness here is saying, and this is on page 5 of the -- of the court record, saying that you came up to him intending to hit him but that when the witness told you to go ahead and hit him, you desisted. Now, did you do that? Did you go up to him and threaten to hit him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say also to this judge "call the police and we'll see if the police dare arrest me"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said something like that, but that's not how I put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you then march out the door, slamming the door shut and damaging it as you left?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could we now move forward to a witness Leila Burekovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the passage that I'm looking at is on page 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Delalic, just excuse me again, we'll find a prompt for the passage that you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So the witness, Mr. Delalic, needs page 5 of the document. It's in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a witness who was a typist who came into the middle of the proceedings, Mr. Delalic, and she said this in her evidence. "When she sat at the typewriter, Judge Hadzic immediately spoke to Celo" -- I'm sorry this is the way it's written here. It says"Celo." It doesn't say "Mr. Delalic," but I'll read from the record. "... immediately spoke to Celo asking him if he wanted to dictate his statement for the record. At that moment, Celo turned towards her and told her to start writing and immediately started dictating. After several sentences, Judge Hadzic interrupted him to explain to him some things. And Celo then turned in the direction of the judge saying 'I already told you not to ask me that. A single word from me and I could go to The Hague for 20 years.'" Do you see that passage in the material before you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's the fact that Mr. Karkin -- sorry, now do you see a bit lower down it says "Karkin started to calm the situation down, but after this Celo started shouting at the judge again and even cursed his mother and insulted him by saying he did not know how to do his job." Now, do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's true -- and that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, there was another indictment against you attached to this indictment, of which you were found not guilty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore I'm going to ask you a very, very brief question about this. That other indictment concerned a threat you made -- sorry, just wait a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to resume, that other indictment that's attached to this one or joined with this one concerned some angry, threatening words you made concerning a man called Ismet Dahic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the allegation put by the Prosecutors, which was found -- on which you were found not guilty was that you had threatened to break Dahic's legs with a baseball bat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, coming to the judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the bottom of page 9 in the English is where I want to go now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Delalic, I'll just take you to the relevant page. Just a moment. I'm sorry, you'll have to forgive the delay once again, but we're just going to identify the spot in the Bosnian transcript for you. Okay. Thank you very much. Mr. Delalic, we're told it's the middle paragraph on page 8 of the Bosnian that you need to look at. Now, this is the section of the judgement where the -- in effect, the judgement is delivered and the Court makes its finding of facts and so on. Do you see a passage where it says, at the bottom, a paragraph this way: "These facts were established beyond doubt in the statement of Witness Ibrahim Hadzic," and it summarises some of the things that he says. Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't repeat everything that is said there, but if you need time or you want something clarified, you may so, of course. But do you see six lines down or five lines down the court goes on to say: "And also of the statement of Nedzad Corovic, and Sabina Bjelak, and Leila Burekovic, who gave identical and convincing statements along the same lines as Ibrahim Hadzic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with this, don't you, that despite what happened the Court agreed with the evidence against you that you did behave the way that those witnesses allege and you did say the things those witnesses claimed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the trial and when the judgement was delivered, none of these witnesses nor Ibrahim Hadzic attended the proceedings. They were never present at the proceedings, so all of this is wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But despite what you say, the court went ahead and found you guilty. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not attend any of the trials. The judge wasn't there, none of the witnesses were there, so the allegations you have made are completely false.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were sentenced in the end to a sentence of six months imprisonment, which was suspended for a period of two years. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. If that's what it says, it must be true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have a final question about the lesser part of the indictment, that concerning the supposed threats to Dahic --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, before counsel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I have been trying in vain to follow this huge document on the thing, and I think Your Honours had made a ruling some time ago that, although we cannot get the documents in advance, we should be provided with a paper copy the moment it's released, so -- and a document of this volume -- because when counsel asked just now what his sentence was, I think I had seen somewhere what it was, but now, of course, I can't immediately look for it. And the witness himself does not remember. And I do not wish -- of course, all the information should be put before Your Honours in an accurate way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: If we could have a copy of all their documents as they produce them in Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that I have followed the proceedings very well according to this e-court system. Secondly, it's a judgement concerning with this witness. If the Defence has possession of that, I assume that it has already been in the possession of the Prosecution long before. I'd check the documents on that trolly and find it. Thirdly, we made a decision on that. If a document is many, many pages, the party using the document is obliged to furnish one to the other party to facilitate the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I say that I have some sympathy for the Prosecutor in this situation. Your Honours will observe that we're going at 100 miles an hour here and I'm happy to provide a copy of that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps in the break which is coming quite soon we'll have a further discussion. There may be some other documents that we can provide. So we'll see what we can do. Could I just ask the court deputy to hand that over now.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I just had a couple of final questions concerning this document. With respect to the -- the accusation that was put -- and I make it clear, you were found not guilty on this crime here. I just have some questions about it. You understand that there were some witnesses claiming that you made this threat to break Ismet Dahic's legs or hit him in the legs with a baseball bat. Do you understand that from looking at this document and from the advice that you received at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive legal advice of any kind. As to what it says here, that I made threats, et cetera, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just on that question of receiving advice, I'll ask you something about that a bit later on. But is it the fact that the police searched your car four days after this event and found a baseball bat there and in fact confiscated that baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The baseball bat was found in my wife's car. It was a very small baseball bat. It wasn't a bat that would be used to make threats with. It was my son's baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your job at that time a debt collector?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you describe yourself in the year 1997 as a debt collector?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a regular company that wasn't involved in forcing people to pay debts, but they would collect debts, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A final question on this document here before I seek to tender it is that at the start of this document it says -- could we just go to page 1 for both the English and the Bosnian. I'm just going to get you to look at the first paragraph here. Do you have that page in front of you now, the first page? Okay. Well, do you see in the first paragraph there it says, and I'm looking really at the last few lines here: "After a public trial held on 15 November 2001 in the presence of the accused, his counsel, Vasvija Vidovic, a lawyer from Sarajevo, and in the absence of the Sarajevo deputy municipal prosecutor, hereby issues the following judgement." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that accurate, despite what you said earlier? Was there a public trial held in the presence of you and your counsel, Vasvija Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's what happened, isn't it? There was a public trial, in fact, and you were really with your lawyer, Vasvija Vidovic, on that occasion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I offer that judgement for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe -- Ms. Chana, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, I'll have to really take this under advisement at this point because I've only got until page 10 and it ends with the sentence: "The court refused to enter the statements as credible because they" -- and I don't know. So I have to during the break see the entire document, Your Honour, and this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry about that. I'll give page 11. Page 11 -- page 11 should be on the -- on the thing, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It ends rather ominously. Now we get page 11. Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that you're not in the position to express your views concerning of this document. We could deal with it at a later stage. I believe it's time for us to take a break, Mr. Morrissey, since you have finished this document, and we'll resume at 1.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Malco Rovcanin there or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Fikret Kajevic there or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Erdin Arnautovic there or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you last speak to Erdin Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the last fortnight?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you spoken to Erdin Arnautovic since you got out of the prison at the end of February?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you spoken to Nedzad Mehanovic since you got out of prison?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the opportunity to see Nedzad Mehanovic because he's in Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to Elvedin Husic since you got out of prison, on the 28th or whenever it was in February?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as to Elvedin Husic, you remain a friend of his. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't really see each other. I haven't seen him for a month or two, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you are on friendly terms with him, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't really have anything to do together, and we don't have any common business and we really see each other very rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you once find yourself charged with a crime with the co-accused Elvedin Husic, a crime involving a man called Daut Basovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you also on another occasion find yourself charged with a crime with the co-accused, and there were three other men accused, but one of them being Nedzad Mehanovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An occasion when you displayed a gun, threatened people at a restaurant called Bezeni and Mr. Mehanovic was charged on the same indictment as possessing certain hand grenades. Do you recall that charge?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that, but it wasn't like that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Well, Mr. Mehanovic was found to be not guilty of the charges. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were found to be guilty, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to six months imprisonment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, now, returning to the finding of the two boys, however. On the occasion when you found those two -- when you first saw those two boys, you're indicating that it was still light. Was that on the afternoon, according to you, of the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And according to you, those boys told you a very distressing story about what had happened to them and to their family. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to you, you were very moved by what they said. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And without any criticism of you, you'd say you were very angry to hear the news of what these boys had been put through. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So therefore, you made inquiries among your men straight away. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For half an hour to an hour I talked to those children. After that, the soldiers who were present, I asked them if anybody knew anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you line them up?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I asked the boys if they could recognise the perpetrators, the people -- of the people who were there, I asked them could they maybe recognise those who did it amongst the people who were there around us in that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you is: Did you line them up?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the boys by the hand and I led them towards the fighters who were there. They were on a meadow, something like that and, holding that boy by the hand, I went from one fighter to the next, asking the boy if he could recognise any of the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the gun in your other hand?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the gun given to you by President Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you line up those fighters or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a classic line-up in the sense that each fighter was standing next to the next one or that it was a line-up in two lines. It was more that the boys went up to each of the fighters to see if they could recognise them. I mean, you could describe that as a line-up if you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's not what I wish, Mr. Delalic. What I'm asking you is: Did you line them up? And your answer is: Well, no, you didn't but you took them from person to person. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since I wasn't really authorised or competent -- it wasn't in my competence to line them up because it wasn't only the fighters from the 9th Motorised Brigade, but there were fighters from some other brigades there, too. I would stop -- I stopped the fighters in what they were doing. They were in the middle of a game or something, and I took the boys and went from one fighter to the next and -- to see if the boy could recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Delalic, I don't -- I wasn't there and I don't mean to quarrel with you about the term "line-up," but this is the occasion, isn't it, when you showed the boys those fighters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't do a line-up on any other occasion, did you, with those boys?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first place where we tried to see if they could recognise anybody was where I saw the boys first. There were several fighters around them and I immediately asked the boys if they could perhaps recognise any of the perpetrators amongst those people. Later, I went to a much larger group of people, and that is also where we tried to see if they could recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after that procedure on that second occasion, you didn't line anyone else up for the boys at Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, my question there has caused trouble, Mr. Delalic. I said "is that correct" and you said "no." Do you mean you didn't line them up again or not? After -- I'll put the question again because I can see there's some hidden confusion that's developed. After that occasion on the meadow when you stopped the men playing and showed them to the boys, did you line anyone else up on any other occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it still light when you did this -- I'll call it "an identification procedure" so that we don't quarrel about -- about it. Did you perform this identification procedure while it was still light or was it getting dark?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For as long as it was still visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you showed the boys to the soldiers on the meadow, it was still daylight. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you then take the boys in a car into Zuka's base at Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it still light or was it getting dark when you got into Zuka's base at Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was still light.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it's after that point that you get the boys an orange juice and you have a conversation with Sefer Halilovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of juice it was, but I did talk to Sefer Halilovic and the others who were also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just to be absolutely clear, this is still on the evening of the 9th of September. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, I put this to you that you have told a false story to this Court about how you dealt with those boys. Do you agree with me or disagree?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The truth is that you kept those boys overnight at the village of Grabovica and you didn't take them in to Jablanica until the next morning. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we've got evidence from one of the boys here about what happened, Mr. Delalic, and he says that's what happened. Do you want to stick to your story that you took him in -- took those boys in on the evening of the 9th to Zuka's base at Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I talked to the children for about an hour. After that, I took them to Zuka's base. It is not true at all that I overnighted with them in Grabovica or spent any time there longer than an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry, counsel. I think there is a protection here, I think it was Witness A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I know. We'll have that redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, well I perhaps -- I apologise for that, Your Honour. It should be -- perhaps I better raise something about that at the end rather than dealing with it now. I'm grateful to the Prosecutor for indicating that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, in any event we've got a problem here, haven't we, Mr. Delalic, because we've got one account saying that you kept them with -- at least one account saying that you kept them in the village until the following day, the morning of the 10th, but you say that you took them in on the evening of the 9th. So I want to ask you this one: You, in the past, have told lies in courts, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I am saying to you is the following: Once I saw the children in an hour or an hour and a half. After that, I took them to the command where Sefer Halilovic and the others were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm referring to page 42 of the date of 1st of February for future reference in terms of transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't the real situation this: You did speak to the boys on the evening of the 9th, but that you didn't perform any line-up procedure until the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm referring to pages 42, 43, and 44 of the transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't that the truth? You kept them there overnight and you showed them some soldiers the next day. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I know you didn't say it. All right. Sorry. What -- just be clear about that -- I'll come to that later on. All right. And your account of giving those boys juice and going in and talking to Halilovic, inspection team members, Bojadzic and Zulfikar Alispago, I put to you, is a fiction made up by you to protect your position. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because in reality, what you did was to bring those children on the morning of the 10th, hand them over to Nihad Bojadzic alone, and then drive Sefko Hodzic, the journalist, into Jablanica. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we have evidence here in this court from the journalist Hodzic as to what he saw you do on that morning, the 10th. His evidence is that you came along in the morning, handed the boys over to Bojadzic, remaining at Donja Jablanica for a very short time, and then took him in, in your car, into Jablanica town. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour -- sorry for interrupting, counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: If counsel is going to refer to testimony of witnesses in the past, which he's quite entitled to do, I think he has to reference the transcript because he cannot summarise like this, like the one -- the transcript he just referred to. So it's quite clear what the particular witness had to say on a certain issue because it's very difficult for -- for myself to go back into that particular witness's evidence to -- to see what was exactly said. So I would request this Chamber to invite the Defence counsel, if they're going to refer to any witness's testimony, to have the pages of the transcript at hand so we can see and they can indicate to the court that that is -- and to the witness and there is the question what another witness has said. It has got to be accurate, Your Honour, otherwise it does not work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe Mr. Morrissey has already informed us about the pages of the transcript. And here we just want to make sure on which date of court was it on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, at the same time you also have to bear in mind the objections from the Prosecution. If possible, you could read these transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honours, could I just indicate -- it's a matter of some importance and frankly the Prosecutor has a good point in some respects. Particularly where a certain word is at issue, I agree, I should have to -- I don't think it's in any doubt that what I've put is the substance of what the witness Hodzic had to say. That was the account that he gave. We will provide the exact transcript references in a moment. Of course, it's a great risk for the Defence if you put it inaccurately because, first of all, you look very bad, and secondly the triumphant Prosecutor will then point it out. So, anyway, Your Honours, I will proceed as I was now, bearing in mind what Your Honour's said and what my learned friend is asking for as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in general terms -- Mr. Delalic, I apologise for that. But in general terms, we've got another problem, haven't we, because Hodzic says one thing and you say another. Now, do you stand firm by your account that you really did take the boys in by -- get them juice, and have that awful discussion with Halilovic, Zuka, and others?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just bearing in mind any conflict between your evidence and that of Mr. Hodzic that might be detected by the Trial Chamber at a later time, when it comes to such conflicts between you and Mr. Hodzic, do you know whether Mr. Sefko Hodzic has ever shot any people in the leg at the Stefanel cafe?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the children were brought to the command or to the IKM, very shortly after that, perhaps after about half an hour, Sefko Hodzic was the first person to interview the children, who told him the story. They told him everything that they had told me. Mr. Sefko Hodzic never passed that story on. So you can then see what kind of a man we're talking about. As far as the shooting, I'm really not interested in whether there was such a shooting or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you may not be interested in whether Mr. Hodzic shot anyone in the leg at the Stefanel cafe. But you did, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The gentleman whom I fired at and who was wounded had served seven years in prison for a rape. During the war he was a deserter, and on several occasions, he was charged of being disorderly, of being violent. There was an -- a warrant out for him, and on that occasion during the war we found him at the Stefanel cafe, and he also was armed. He had a gun on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there another man that you shot at the Stefanel cafe in the leg?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you shoot at another man's feet and he accidentally got a ricocheted bullet in the leg at the Stefanel cafe?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just dealing with the Sefko Hodzic issue, did Sefko Hodzic ever travel on a false passport, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me silly things. Could you please ask me a specific question. I'm really not interested whether Sefko Hodzic travelled with a false passport or whether he fired at anyone. Could you please ask me something else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you the questions that I want to ask you, thanks. My next question is: You're effectively, I suggest to you, smearing the character of Sefko Hodzic because you know that his evidence could possibly hurt you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't that a tactic of yours, to smear anyone who can hurt you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say yesterday that -- who was the commander of the 1st Corps? Perhaps I'll stop the questioning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, we might have a problem with the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm afraid even I can't think of a conspiracy concerning that one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Might I just inquire whether I'm the only one whose system is down or whether everyone is -- everyone's in trouble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think everything is okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, we'll just wait until we've got the -- okay. Thank you. Your Honours, I've just been provided with the relevant transcript and I think I'll -- because of my friend's question I better put it. Your Honours, we're dealing with the 23rd of March, and this is in relation to -- to the Hodzic testimony. We're dealing with the 23rd of March, 2005, at pages 79, 80, 81, and 82 for completeness's sake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm afraid that you have to wait for a few minutes. Can you try?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Delalic, we're going to attempt another question here. Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, it's gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I indicate something very briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think it's likely we go into Friday with this witness. I intend to do my best to finish him by the weekend, so I indicate that so he can make the plans he has to make. That's my intention. Just a timing comment to fill up time, really, Your Honour. My apologies, but it could be of relevance in terms of whether we adjourn for now because we're not going to finish him tomorrow. I think it's very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you suggest that we adjourn now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm in the Court's hands. I'm very happy standing. But, Your Honours, it may just be -- as we only have 13 minutes left, I'm happy to suggest that we adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I see no objections from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour, we are in the Court's hands as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, I believe you still remember what I told you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So the hearing for today is adjourned. We'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
